Good to Talk · Free. Always.

Stress and overwhelm

Written and researched by Matt O’Brien, founder of Shift Some Timber.

Need urgent help?

If you or someone else is in danger, call 999 or go to A&E. In England, if you need urgent mental-health help but it is not an emergency, use NHS 111 online or call 111 and select the mental-health option.

See current NHS urgent mental-health support →

Urgent support across the UK

Stress isn't a personal failure. Sometimes there are simply more demands than you've currently got capacity for.

Stress can show up everywhere

NHS guidance notes that stress can affect how you feel physically and mentally and how you behave. Examples include difficulty concentrating, feeling overwhelmed, constant worry, irritability, sleeping differently, eating differently, avoiding people or places, and drinking or smoking more.

Do a pressure audit

Write down what's currently taking up headspace. Mark each item: act, ask for help, accept for now, or not mine to carry. It sounds simple; the point is to get ten simultaneous problems out of your head and onto something you can see.

When stress is running your life

If you're struggling to cope, symptoms are persistent, or stress is significantly affecting daily life, speak to your GP or use appropriate NHS support. Chest pain or other concerning physical symptoms should not simply be assumed to be stress.
